question.problem:
The signed curvature of the plane curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-{t}^{2}⟩$ is given by

$$
k(t)=\frac{2\cdot (\,\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,)}{\sqrt{({cos}^{2}⁡t+4{t}^{2})^{3}}}.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.worked_solution:
The signed curvature $k(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t)⟩$ is given by

$$
k(t)=\frac{{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y(t)=-{t}^{2}.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =-2t \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the signed curvature, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}k(t) & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-2)-(-2t)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}{{((\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-2t)^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{({cos}^{2}⁡t+4{t}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}{\sqrt{({cos}^{2}⁡t+4{t}^{2})^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$
